title: G-Drive wins the ELMS opener as the pole-sitter crashes out
dek: Tincknell, Dolan and van der Garde won the 4 Hours of Silverstone in the G-Drive Gibson #38, about a minute and a half clear, after pole-sitting Thiriet by TDS crashed out early.

chapters.title: A big prototype grid for round one
text: The 2016 European Le Mans Series opened at Silverstone on 16 April with the 4 Hours of Silverstone, the first round of a season that would run to six races. The entry was 44 cars, and the headline in the top class was its size: 16 LMP2-spec cars, a count that included the Morgan #84 of SRT41 by OAK Racing, the Garage 56 project heading for Le Mans. Four teams were making their series debut in the class: DragonSpeed, SO24! by Lombard Racing, Panis Barthez Competition and IDEC Sport.

Among the favourites, G-Drive Racing, the rebranded Jota operation, ran the Gibson #38 for Simon Dolan, Harry Tincknell and Giedo van der Garde and was hungry to win the title after several near-misses. Greaves Motorsport arrived as defending champion with a new Ligier JS P2 and a new line-up of Rojas, Canal and Giermaziak. Thiriet by TDS Racing, whose 2015 title bid had fallen short, paired Pierre Thiriet and Ryo Hirakawa with Mathias Beche, on loan from the Rebellion LMP1 squad. SMP Racing ran two BR 01s, with the #32 for Coletti, Leal and Wirth and a late race-by-race #44 for Gelael, Evans and Giovinazzi. Krohn Racing had Bjorn Wirdheim, the reigning LMP2 champion, standing in for Olivier Pla, and Sir Chris Hoy was making his LMP2 debut with Algarve Pro Racing ahead of Le Mans. Murphy Prototypes only confirmed Damien Faulkner, Shaun Balfe and Sean Doyle for its Oreca #48 on the eve of the meeting.

Friday belonged to Thiriet by TDS. Beche topped a wet opening session, and in the afternoon he set 1:49.320, the only lap under 1:50 and more than two seconds clear of the DragonSpeed Oreca. G-Drive had the opposite day. A gearbox problem cost the Gibson most of its running, and Tincknell was nominated to qualify as Silverstone was his home track. The weather stayed unsettled, with snow on Saturday morning before the field gridded up for a dry race.

chapters.title: Beche takes pole on a wet track
text: Qualifying was run on a wet track and was interrupted by a red flag when Faulkner put the Murphy Oreca into the gravel at Luffield. Beche was the only driver to set a flying lap early on and his 2:06.471 in the Thiriet by TDS Oreca #46 stood as pole position, completing a weekend in which the French team had topped every session. He was out on track first and did not need to improve once the session resumed.

Stefano Coletti put the SMP Racing BR 01 #32 second, 1.105 seconds slower on 2:07.576, and Leo Roussel took the Pegasus Racing Morgan #29 to third with 2:07.624. Tincknell was fourth for G-Drive on 2:07.855, ahead of Nicolas Lapierre in the DragonSpeed Oreca #21. Gelael in the second SMP car was sixth and Giermaziak seventh for Greaves. A yellow at the end of the session, when Parth Ghorpade spun the Algarve Pro Ligier at Club, spoiled the final laps of several drivers.

chapters.title: Pole-sitter out, Tincknell leads
text: The start was chaotic. Roussel's Pegasus Morgan #29 speared sideways into the wall by the pits as the lights went out and limped back to the garage with front-end damage. Pierre Thiriet ran wide at the first corner and dropped away from pole, which let Andreas Wirth lead the opening lap in the SMP car. Tincknell, who had started fourth, had the better exit from the Complex, passed the BR 01 on the Wellington Straight and was 3.6 seconds clear after four laps.

Paul-Loup Chatin carved his way up in the Panis Barthez Ligier #23, passing Wirth on lap seven, and the Ligier would set the fastest lap of the race. Meanwhile Wirdheim moved the Krohn Ligier into third. Tincknell was about 40 seconds clear when disaster struck further back. Thiriet, trying to recover, slid into the barrier at Luffield, and the Eurasia Oreca #33 of Tristan Gommendy stopped at the same corner. Both cars retired and the full-course yellow cut the gap to around 25 seconds. By the end of the hour Chatin was closing again, with most of the front runners staying out for their first stops.

chapters.title: Barthez leads before G-Drive takes control
text: The first round of stops left Tincknell more than 22 seconds ahead of Chatin, but the lead changed hands when the Gibson came in for Dolan. Chatin had stretched his stint to 48 laps before handing the Ligier to team co-owner Fabien Barthez, who went to the front, while Chris Hoy spun the Algarve Pro Ligier and the resulting full-course yellow shaped the stops. Quadruple amputee Frederic Sausset climbed into the SRT41 Morgan for his first ELMS stint, a step on the road to Le Mans.

Dolan then reeled Barthez in, closing to under ten seconds around lap 60 and passing him without drama by lap 66, shortly after half distance. From there he built an 11.5-second lead and G-Drive never looked back. Behind them, Canal had moved the Greaves Ligier #41 up to third as the Panis Barthez car handed to Timothe Buret, and Coletti and Evans ran in line astern in the two SMP cars. As the third hour went on, rain clouds drifted towards the circuit, but no downpour came.

chapters.title: Panis Barthez fades, SMP and SO24! move up
text: Spots of rain fell in the last hour without producing a wet race. Giermaziak pitted twice in the Greaves Ligier, the second stop turning into a garage visit, which dropped the car out of the podium places and into eighth at the flag. The Panis Barthez Ligier, so strong all day, then came into the International pit lane with a clear mechanical problem. Buret lost a lot of time resetting the car, rejoined and stopped again, and the car finished ninth. Coletti inherited second place, and when Evans stopped for the last time, Olivier Lombard moved the SO24! by Lombard Ligier #22 briefly to second before its own stop restored Coletti.

In the closing stages Niclas Jonsson passed Evans for fourth, putting the Krohn Ligier ahead of the second SMP Racing car. The Pegasus Morgan, already damaged at the start, lost a rear wheel with about 20 minutes left, which brought out a full-course yellow.

chapters.title: G-Drive wins by a minute and a half
text: Dolan's long middle stint was followed by van der Garde, who took over with roughly 40 minutes to go and brought the Gibson home after 118 laps, about a minute and a half clear of Coletti. It was a winning debut for the Dutchman in a G-Drive car: van der Garde said afterwards that it was his first race of this kind, that he had to learn to deal with traffic, and that winning straight away after a year away from racing felt fantastic.

SMP Racing's #32 (Coletti, Leal, Wirth) finished second on the same lap, and SO24! by Lombard Racing (Capillaire, Lombard, Coleman) completed the podium one lap down after a weekend that had gone badly for the team beforehand. Krohn Racing (Krohn, Jonsson, Wirdheim) was fourth and the second SMP car (Gelael, Evans, Giovinazzi) fifth, with Race Performance sixth and IDEC Sport seventh, both two laps down. Neither Thiriet by TDS nor Eurasia was classified.

chapters.title: G-Drive banks 25 points, TDS leaves empty-handed
text: G-Drive left Silverstone with the 25 points for a win, a strong start to its LMP2 title bid. Tincknell described the race as intense but remarkably clean, said that the team had been disappointed in qualifying and that getting ahead and driving away was the key, and praised Dolan and van der Garde for their stints. He had little time to celebrate: he was due in the WEC Ford GT the next day.

Behind the winners, SMP Racing had both BR 01s in the top five, with Coletti, Leal and Wirth second. SO24! by Lombard Racing took the final podium place, a welcome result in its first ELMS LMP2 race. Krohn Racing took a strong fourth with Wirdheim, who would be replaced by Pla from round two, and defending champions Greaves Motorsport had to settle for eighth after Giermaziak's two stops. Hoy finished tenth on his LMP2 debut with Algarve Pro Racing. The big losers were Thiriet by TDS, who had led every session and started from pole but finished with nothing, and Panis Barthez, who lost a likely podium to a mechanical problem after Chatin's fastest lap of 1:50.426.
The result was also a milestone for Sausset, who finished 31st in the SRT41 Morgan, 12 laps behind the winner, in his first ELMS race, with the Garage 56 car heading to Le Mans in June.
The European Le Mans Series now moves to Italy for the 4 Hours of Imola on 15 May.

facts.v: Sixteen LMP2-spec cars started the season opener, with four teams making their LMP2 debut in the series.
